land.text: the whole duchy, annexed by Prussia in 1866 and from 1868 part of the province of Hesse-Nassau

capitals.name: Wiesbaden
capitals.note: Infobox: Wiesbaden (1816-1866); 'Weilburg ceased to be capital, and Wiesbaden became the sole capital' in 1816.

rulers.title: Sovereign Duke of Nassau
rulers.note: 30 August 1806 to 24 March 1816; Frederick William of Nassau-Weilburg took the title Sovereign Prince in July 1806.

rulers.name: Adolphe
rulers.title: Duke
rulers.note: 20 August 1839 to 20 September 1866; later Grand Duke of Luxembourg (1890).

keyframe_review.note: German Confederation page table: Nassau 4,700 km2 (no year). Cliopatria's outline (11,345 km2) sits about 30 km too far west of the duchy. Cell test on the v0.2.1 geometry (this repair, confirming the reviewer's point-in-polygon test): no cell of the shape holds Weilburg (the capital to 1816), Limburg, Idstein, Usingen, Königstein, Höchst or Wiesbaden, and the left bank of the Rhine (Koblenz, Boppard, Andernach, Bingen) and the Bonn-Sieg country to the north are inside it. The corrected shape is drawn from the towns the pages name (Duchy page: Rheingau, Höchst, Königstein, Cronberg, Lahnstein, Kaub, Eppstein, Braubach, Ehrenbreitstein, Vallendar, Sayn, Montabaur, Limburg; German page: Usingen received 'Höchst, Königstein, Cronberg, Lahnstein und den Rheingau', Weilburg 'Ehrenbreitstein').  The 1806, 1809 and 1811 outlines also carry a lobe north to 52.7 N (6.4-7.9 E, Westphalia) that no page supports, and 302,769 inhabitants in 1806 do not fit 11,345 km2. The corrected shape is 19 grid cells (about 4,807 km2 at 253 km2 a cell, ratio 1.02 to the table); the Rhine bank cannot be split from the cell opposite it, so Koblenz and Bingen still fall in the cells of Ehrenbreitstein and the Rheingau.

After the exchange of 31 May-1 June 1815 the corrected shape drops Neuwied, Dierdorf and Altenkirchen (Prussian from 1815: Wied-Neuwied page '1815 fielen beide wiedischen Territorien an Preußen'; Altenkirchen page 'Mit dem Wiener Kongress 1815 fiel Sayn-Altenkirchen ... an Preußen') and adds Dillenburg, Herborn, Hadamar and Diez (Nassau-Oranien page: '1813 und endgültig im Wiener Kongress 1815 kamen die Fürstentümer ... Katzenelnbogen town is already inside the drawn duchy from 1806 (the Duchy page has Nassau-Usingen receiving it from Hesse-Darmstadt in 1803; the German page has the Niedergrafschaft in the 1815 exchange), so that part of the exchange changes no cell. 19 grid cells, about 4,807 km2, ratio 1.02 to the 4,700 km2 of the German Confederation page. The 1815 Cliopatria shape (1815-1819) is five cells larger than the corrected one because it keeps the left bank.

region.text: das Fürstentum Wied-Neuwied, 'dem Herzogtum Nassau zugeschlagen'

ledger.note: 1806: the Principality of Wied-Neuwied is dissolved under Napoleon's pressure and assigned to the Duchy of Nassau. 'wurde das Fürstentum 1806 auf Druck des französischen Kaisers Napoléon aufgelöst und dem Herzogtum Nassau zugeschlagen' (Wied-Neuwied page). No month is given; the dossier county-of-wied (eu-09, 1093-1806) names Nassau as its successor.

region.text: the Duchy of Nassau 1806-1814 as the pages name it: the Rheingau, Höchst, Königstein, Cronberg, Lahnstein, Ehrenbreitstein, Limburg, Weilburg, Montabaur, Idstein and Usingen, Sayn-Altenkirchen and Sayn-Hachenburg, and from 1806 Wied-Neuwied; circles on the pages' towns, not Cliopatria's outline, which sits about 30 km too far west

ledger.note: 1806: Nassau-Usingen and Nassau-Weilburg merge into the Duchy of Nassau on 30 August 1806. 'Under pressure from Napoleon I both counties merged to form the Duchy of Nassau on 30 August 1806'; both had joined the Confederation of the Rhine in July (17 July on the Duchy and German pages, 12 July on the Confederation page). The page names the lands won in 1803-1804, not a boundary. The region is redrawn on the towns the pages name (repair of the reviewer's finding); Cliopatria's outline is about 30 km too far west.

region.text: die Fürstentümer der oranischen Linie, Nassau-Diez, Nassau-Hadamar und Nassau-Dillenburg

ledger.note: 1815: the Orange-Nassau principalities of Dillenburg, Hadamar and Diez come to the Duchy. '1813 und endgültig im Wiener Kongress 1815 kamen die Fürstentümer der oranischen Linie, Nassau-Diez, Nassau-Hadamar und Nassau-Dillenburg' to the Walramian line (Nassau-Oranien page); the Duchy page: the Orange line surrendered its principality to Prussia, 'which passed part of it to the Duchy of Nassau the next day' (1 June 1815). The counterpart is Prussia as the intermediary; the Nassau-Oranien page does not name Herborn. The month of the Congress allocation is not given.

region.text: '1815 fielen beide wiedischen Territorien an Preußen'

ledger.note: 1815: Wied-Neuwied, held by Nassau since 1806, falls to Prussia. '1815 fielen beide wiedischen Territorien an Preußen' (Wied-Neuwied page); the family's holdings became a Standesherrschaft under Prussian sovereignty. The month is not given; kingdom-of-prussia (eu-09) has no matching gain.

region.text: Sayn-Altenkirchen, 'Kreis Altenkirchen im preußischen Regierungsbezirk Koblenz'

ledger.note: 1815: Sayn-Altenkirchen, which Nassau held from 1803 (Reichsdeputationshauptschluss of 25 February 1803), goes to Prussia. 'Mit dem Wiener Kongress 1815 fiel Sayn-Altenkirchen mit weiten Teilen von Sayn-Hachenburg' to Prussia, 'ging als Kreis Altenkirchen im preußischen Regierungsbezirk Koblenz auf' (Altenkirchen page). The page does not say whether Hachenburg town went too; the drawn duchy keeps the Hachenburg cell (confidence 1 for that cell).

region.text: die Niedergrafschaft Katzenelnbogen (a 15 km circle round Katzenelnbogen; the place is not in the gazetteer)

ledger.note: 1815: Nassau receives the Niedergrafschaft Katzenelnbogen. After the Orange-Nassau line took the Dutch crown (31 May 1815) and ceded its homelands to Prussia, 'Am Folgetag gab Preußen einen Teil davon an Nassau weiter. Dabei ... erhielt [Nassau] die Niedergrafschaft Katzenelnbogen' (the Duchy page: Prussia 'passed part of it to the Duchy of Nassau the next day', 1 June 1815). The gazetteer lacks Katzenelnbogen; the circle (7.96 E 50.22 N) is a placement. Conflict: the Duchy page has Nassau-Usingen already receiving Katzenelnbogen from Hesse-Darmstadt in 1803. Katzenelnbogen town is already drawn from 1806 (see the 1815 keyframe), so this event changes no cell; the region is kept as the page's word for what was passed on.

union.text: Grenzstreifen nahe Siegen (on the Nassau side, between Dillenburg and Siegen)
Grenzstreifen nahe Wetzlar (on the Nassau side, between Weilburg and Wetzlar)

region.text: Grenzstreifen nahe Siegen und Wetzlar (two 6 km circles on the Nassau side of the border, moved off Siegen and Wetzlar themselves)

ledger.note: 1815: Nassau gives border strips near Siegen and Wetzlar to Prussia in the same exchange: 'Dabei gab Nassau Grenzstreifen nahe Siegen und Wetzlar an Preußen ab'. Wetzlar was a Prussian exclave east of Nassau; the circles are placements on the Nassau side of the border (moved in the repair; Siegen and Wetzlar themselves were Prussian), the strips' size is not given.
1816: Weilburg ceases to be the capital and Wiesbaden becomes the sole capital (Duchy page infobox: 'Weilburg (1806-1816); Wiesbaden (1816-1866)').

1866: Prussia occupies the duchy. 'After being occupied and annexed into the Kingdom of Prussia in 1866 following the Austro-Prussian War' (Duchy page); the Austro-Prussian War page (14 June - 22 July 1866) is silent on Nassau and the German page has only the skirmish at Zorn near Wiesbaden on 12 July 1866, so the month is unknown.

1866: the occupation ends in annexation, promulgated on 20 September 1866 ('Am 16. August 1866 ... die Absicht, Hannover, Hessen-Kassel, Nassau und die Stadt Frankfurt am Main' to unite with Prussia; German page). The dissolve event below carries the annexation.

region.text: the whole duchy, annexed by Prussia

ledger.note: 1866: Prussia annexes the Duchy of Nassau on 20 September 1866. German Confederation page: 'Hanover, Hesse-Kassel, Nassau, Frankfurt, and Hesse-Homburg: 20 September 1866'; Duke Adolphe's reign ends 20 September 1866 (Duchy page). The Duchy page's infobox says 'Annexed by Prussia on 23 August 1866' (the date of the Peace of Prague, which does not name Nassau); the German page: announced 16 August, law of 20 September 1866. Nassau and Frankfurt became the Wiesbaden district of the Prussian province of Hesse-Nassau (1868).

wars.name: War of the Sixth Coalition
wars.outcome: Nassau, a member of the Confederation of the Rhine, changed sides on 23 November 1813 and was guaranteed its 'souveränes Fortbestehen' by Russia, Austria and Prussia; the Congress of Vienna settled its boundary in 1815.
wars.note: The Sixth Coalition article was not opened; the page wording is the German Duchy page's. The Confederation of the Rhine was dissolved on 4 November 1813 (Confederation page).

wars.name: Austro-Prussian War

zones.text: the duchy, occupied and annexed after the war

wars.outcome: 'When the Austro-Prussian War broke out on 14 June 1866, the Duchy of Nassau took the side of Austria'; the Peace of Prague was dated 23 August 1866 and Prussia annexed Nassau on 20 September 1866.
wars.note: The German page: the skirmish at Zorn on 12 July 1866 was called a Nassau 'Sieg'. The Duchy page: 'occupied and annexed into the Kingdom of Prussia in 1866 following the Austro-Prussian War' (no month); the Austro-Prussian War page (infobox 14 June - 22 July 1866) is silent on Nassau, so the occupation is dated to the year only (ledger).

certainty.note: The duchy was assembled from many small mediatised holdings in 1803-1806 and consolidated into three districts only on 1 August 1809 (German page); no page gives a boundary.
The 1815 exchange with Prussia (Katzenelnbogen, the strips near Siegen and Wetzlar) is the last boundary change on the pages; the Wetzlar exclave of Prussia remained to the east.

notes: REPAIR (batch eu-20-e, 2026-11-01). Cliopatria's Nassau outline (every shape 1806-1865) sits about 30 km too far west: no cell holds Weilburg, Limburg, Idstein, Usingen, Königstein, Höchst or Wiesbaden, and it covers the left bank of the Rhine and the Bonn-Sieg country (reviewer's point-in-polygon test; my cell test agrees). All nine keyframes are therefore adjust with a shape drawn from lon/lat circles on the towns the pages name: 19 cells (about 4,807 km2) in both periods (Neuwied, Dierdorf and Altenkirchen in 1806-1814, Dillenburg, Herborn and Hadamar from 1815), against the 4,700 km2 of the German Confederation page. DISAGREEMENT with the reviewer's recipe (minus the left bank, union circles): about a third of the 1807 cells are the Bonn-Sieg lobe and the Moselle bank, which would need three more cuts, so the shape is built on circles alone. Resolution: the grid cell (253 km2, 17 km across) cannot split the Rhine, so Koblenz, Bingen, Mainz and Frankfurt (Höchst) fall in cells whose centre is on the Nassau side. New facts from pages: Wied-Neuwied 1806-1815 (Wied-Neuwied page), Sayn-Altenkirchen 1803-1815 (Altenkirchen page), the Orange-Nassau principalities Dillenburg, Hadamar, Diez in 1815 (Nassau-Oranien page; Herborn is not named there), the Prussian occupation in 1866 (year only). The step +441 km2 from the 1815 to the 1820 Cliopatria shape (one cell) is still unexplained by any page and is not carried. DISAGREEMENTS between pages: Confederation join 12 July (Confederation page) or 17 July (Duchy and German pages); annexation 23 August (Duchy infobox) or 20 September (German Confederation page, German page's law); Katzenelnbogen in 1803 (Duchy page, from Hesse-Darmstadt) or 1815 (German page, Niedergrafschaft). The Peace of Prague page does not mention Nassau. GAZETTEER: Katzenelnbogen, Siegen, Wetzlar, Weilburg, Limburg an der Lahn, Idstein, Dillenburg, Neuwied, Altenkirchen are not in the gazetteer (circles). The 1806 Wied-Neuwied gain uses the existing dossier county-of-wied (eu-09, ends 1806, names Nassau as successor); the 1815 Orange-Nassau lands are covered by principality-of-nassau-orange-fulda only in part. Pages budget: 5 original plus 4 in the repair (Nassau-Oranien, Wied-Neuwied, Altenkirchen, Austro-Prussian War).
